clauses.text:
1. The several executive departments,  
independent establishments, and other  
governmental agencies in the District of  
Columbia, including the Government  
Printing Office and the Navy Yard and  
Naval Stations, shall be closed all day on  
Tuesday, December 24,1940, the day pre­
ceding Christmas Day; and all employees  
in the Federal service in the District of  
Columbia, and in the field service of the  
executive departments, independent es­
tablishments, and other agencies of the  
Government, except those who may for  
special public reasons be excluded from  
the provisions of this order by the heads  
of their respective departments, estab­
lishments, or agencies, or those whose  
absence from duty would be inconsistent  
with the provisions of existing law, shall  
be excused from duty on that day.

2. This order shall be published in the  
F ederal R egister.

EXECUTIVE ORDER
Excusing F ederal E mployees F rom D uty 
on D ecember 24, 1940
By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in me as President of the  
United States, it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1. The several executive departments,  
independent establishments, and other  
governmental agencies in the District of  
Columbia, including the Government  
Printing Office and the Navy Yard and  
Naval Stations, shall be closed all day on  
Tuesday, December 24,1940, the day pre­
ceding Christmas Day; and all employees  
in the Federal service in the District of  
Columbia, and in the field service of the  
executive departments, independent es­
tablishments, and other agencies of the  
Government, except those who may for  
special public reasons be excluded from  
the provisions of this order by the heads  
of their respective departments, estab­
lishments, or agencies, or those whose  
absence from duty would be inconsistent  
with the provisions of existing law, shall  
be excused from duty on that day.
2. This order shall be published in the  
F ederal R egister.
F ranklin D R oosevelt
T he W hite  H ouse,
December 16, 1940.
[No. 8613]
[F. R . Doc. 40-5680; Filed, D ecem ber 17, 1940;
9:29 a. m .]

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 8613 of December 16, 1940 (5 FR 5143, Federal Register issue of December 18, 1940) closed executive departments and agencies in the District of Columbia and excused federal employees from duty on Tuesday, December 24, 1940, and directed its own publication in the Federal Register. Both clauses were spent by their own terms: clause 2 was performed when the order was published in the Federal Register issue dated December 18, 1940 (the filing line reads December 17, 1940), and clause 1 applied to the single calendar day December 24, 1940 and had no further subject after that day. The end date for clause 1 is recorded as December 24, 1940 inclusive (the order runs through that day); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when December 24 begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. No instrument held in the repository revokes, extends or amends the order. The working text is the official Federal Register page text (machine-extracted from the PDF, OCR), not an authenticated transcription.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end for clause 1: it is a one-day closure and excusal, with no revocation, extension or amendment in the held record (no later-event chain events; zero hits in the U.S. Code, eCFR and Office of the Federal Register disposition-note searches; the bounded held-text search found no later order citing it by number). A report-style deadline is not at issue; the day named is the order's own period. Clause 2 ended earlier, on performance: the held Federal Register page for 5 FR 5143 is the issue headed \"Washington, Wednesday, December 18, 1940\" and carries the order, which shows the direction to publish was carried out by December 18, 1940. The whole order therefore ended on the later of the two, December 24, 1940.","independent_command_check":"No independent command exists. The exceptions in paragraph 1 qualify the closure and excusal for December 24, 1940 only; they confer no standing power. Paragraph 2 is a one-time publication direction, performed on publication.","savings_check":"The order has no savings clause. Employees' excused absence on December 24, 1940 is an accrued past consequence of the executed closure, not a continuing command; no held source shows any pending right or duty beyond that day.","scope_check":"Clause inventory confirmed against the whole held order: heading, the introductory authority recital, paragraph 1 (the closure and the excusal of employees, with its exceptions for employees excluded by agency heads or whose absence would be inconsistent with existing law) and paragraph 2 (publication), then the signature, date and filing line. The packet's two clauses correspond to paragraphs 1 and 2 exactly. The excusal and the exceptions are one sentence of paragraph 1 and share its end."}

savings_residuals.reason: The excusal from duty on December 24, 1940 accrued to employees on that day. That consequence is a surviving effect of the executed closure, not a continuing command of Executive Order 8613; the order has no savings clause and the held searches show no later instrument touching it.
